newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Court offers journalist freedom pending trial.
newsitem.headline: Court offers journalist freedom pending trial.

text.p: Zaire's Supreme Court offered a journalist charged with spreading false rumours about President Mobutu Sese Seko's health his provisional freedom on Friday pending trial, court sources said.
Michel Luya, owner and publisher of Le Palmares, would be freed on provision of $2,500 bail, the sources added.
Hundreds of journalists marched through Kinshasa before the verdict demanding Luya's release.
Luya has been in detention since September 17 in connection with an article saying Mobutu was riddled with cancer and would have an operation for throat cancer.
Mobutu had a prostate operation in Switzerland on August 22 and his entourage say he is expected to return home next month.
Luya has been indicted to stand trial for spreading false rumours, a charge carrying a sentence of one to 12 months in jail. No trial date has been fixed. Luya has pleaded not guilty.
The government suspended Le Palmares for an indefinite period. The newspaper was suspended for three months in 1993 over a cartoon of Mobutu.
